cards.definitions: Graphs are finite, undirected and simple. A minor is obtained by deleting vertices or edges and contracting edges, with loops removed and parallel edges suppressed. An H-minor model in G consists of pairwise disjoint connected vertex sets B_v for v∈V(H), with an edge between B_u and B_v for each uv∈E(H); its support is their union. Let pack_H(G) be the largest number of models with mutually disjoint supports, and let τ_H(G) be the minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves no H minor. The integral Erdős–Pósa property on C means that a function f:N_0→N_0 exists such that τ_H(G)≤f(pack_H(G)) for every G∈C. This one f may depend on H and C, but not on the individual graph. A class is minor-closed if it contains every minor of each of its graphs. A graph parameter is invariant under graph isomorphism and is minor-monotone when G′ a minor of G implies p_H(G′)≤p_H(G). Boundedness on C means one finite bound for all graphs in C. H need not be connected. No efficient evaluation algorithm or uniquely prescribed parameter is part of the conjecture.
cards.answer_criterion: The affirmative answer follows from the published finite obstruction-sequence characterization: for the target class of H-minor-free graphs, take p_H(G) to be the largest order of an obstruction in its fixed finite collection of increasing minor sequences that occurs as a minor of G, using 0 when none occurs. Minor monotonicity and the theorem’s excluded-sequence criterion give exactly the required equivalence.

context_blocks.text: VC dimension characterizes nonprivate learning. Finite Littlestone dimension $\mathrm{LD}$ characterizes the existence of private learning but does not determine its optimal quantitative cost.

A sample-complexity characterization should tell us how many labelled examples are necessary from the structure of the hypothesis class, rather than from a particular learning algorithm. Two classes can have the same ordinary capacity measure while differing in how difficult it is to hide the influence of an individual training example.

The quantitative issue matters even after learnability is settled. Knowing that some finite sample size works does not distinguish a useful bound from an enormous one. The proposed relation asks whether the extra price of privacy can be controlled by ordinary statistical complexity together with a very slowly growing function of online-learning complexity.

cards.definitions: A concept class is a finite set of functions from a domain X to {0,1}. VC(C) is the largest size of a subset of X on which all binary labelings occur. LD(C) is the greatest depth of a complete binary tree labeled by domain points such that every root-to-leaf edge-label sequence is realized by a concept. The function log-star counts base-two logarithms needed to reach at most one. A learner may output a hypothesis outside C. Privacy requires $\Pr[A(S)\in E]\le e\Pr[A(S\prime)\in E]+1/(100m^2)$ whenever the two m-record samples differ by replacement of one record. Here X is finite, distributions on X are arbitrary probability vectors, and a learner is a probability kernel from length-m labeled samples to the finite set {0,1}^X of hypotheses. The sample size m is a positive integer chosen for C before the target and distribution. For every target h∈C and distribution D on X, with probability at least 9/10 over m independent draws x_i from D and learner randomness, the returned hypothesis has D-probability of disagreement with h at most 1/10. Privacy holds for all labeled samples, including unrealizable ones, and all subsets E of the hypothesis set. The same kernel and m work for all D,h. This finite-domain convention retains the finite-class target: points in an arbitrary domain with the same label vector (h(x))_{h∈C} can be identified, giving at most 2^|C| cells and preserving both dimensions. A learner on those cells lifts to the original domain. No running-time or computable-representation requirement is imposed.

Nikolov’s August 2022 preprint, published at SODA 2023 and subsequently in the Journal of Privacy and Confidentiality, gives the requested pure-private normalized Euclidean guarantee. Theorem 1 explicitly identifies its conclusion as the resolution of Nikolov–Ullman Open Problem 2. The source proposal was therefore stale when imported.

A statistical query is a bounded average. For a database of categories, an indicator query asks what fraction of records belong to a selected set of categories. Several queries can ask about overlapping sets, so their answers concern the same individuals. Privacy constrains the distribution of the entire released vector under replacement of any one record. Protecting each coordinate separately with the full privacy budget would not establish the required joint guarantee.

The normalized Euclidean error is the square root of the average squared coordinate error for one output, followed by expectation over the mechanism. If the error vector is (1,0,…,0), its normalized Euclidean error is 1/√k, whereas its maximum-coordinate error is one. Thus one badly estimated query can have much less effect on the average criterion. The position of the expectation also matters: this is not the square root of the expected squared error.

The 2021 question sought a bound independent of k, the number of queries. Its shifted logarithm handles a singleton universe, and the minimum with one reflects a trivial data-independent release: outputting the zero vector has normalized error at most one. A singleton universe in fact permits exact release, because all databases have the same answer vector. These conventions do not assert a matching lower bound in every parameter regime.

Nikolov proves sample complexity O(log T/(εα²)) for normalized error α, alongside sharper alternatives for some parameters. Rearranging gives the square-root accuracy bound. His definitions use bounded real queries, replacement adjacency and the expected norm divided by √k, matching this card. The mechanism exploits a lower-dimensional representation of the feasible answer vectors and also has an efficiency guarantee beyond this card’s existence requirement.

The July 2026 version of Fitzsimons’s paper focused on the maximum-coordinate problem and retained a √log(2k) factor. Its 3 August revision adds Theorem 1.2 with the exact Euclidean rate and explicitly acknowledges Nikolov’s earlier solution. The Euclidean conclusion therefore must not be classified as still open by reading only the first version or the abstract-page summary. The newer paper’s claimed formalization was not independently built or audited here.

cards.definitions: Let X be an instance domain and H⊆{0,1}^X. Before learning starts, an oblivious adversary fixes h*∈H and x_1,…,x_T∈X, with labels y_t=h*(x_t). In round t the randomized learner outputs a hypothesis h_t:X→{0,1} using only its previous observations, then receives (x_t,y_t); its mistake count is Σ_t 1[h_t(x_t)≠y_t]. The guarantee is a worst-case bound on the expectation over the learner’s randomness. Pure ε-differential privacy means that for any two length-T labeled sequences S,S′ differing in one example and any event E of full output sequences, Pr[A(S)∈E]≤e^ε Pr[A(S′)∈E]. This privacy condition applies to all labeled sequences, including unrealizable ones. A probabilistic representation of H is a distribution P over finite sets V of binary hypotheses such that, for every h*∈H and every distribution D on X, with probability at least 3/4 over V∼P some v∈V has Pr_{x∼D}[v(x)≠h*(x)]≤1/4. Its size is the largest log|V| in its support, and RepDim(H) is the infimum of these sizes. Finite representation dimension is the class condition characterizing pure private PAC learnability. The target o(T) is for each fixed H and ε as T tends to infinity, uniformly over the realizable oblivious sequences; it does not mean a finite mistake bound independent of T.
cards.answer_criterion: The published affirmative theorem establishes an ε-private learner with expected mistake bound O(log²T·(RepDim(H)+log log T)²/ε) for large T, which is o(T) for every fixed finite RepDim(H) and ε>0. The result is information-theoretic and applies to oblivious realizable sequences.
